title: JC H2 biology — cell: ultrastructure and biomolecules
subject: science

flashcards.back: A selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer with drifting proteins (the fluid mosaic): hydrophilic heads face water, hydrophobic tails face inward.
The control centre storing DNA as chromatin, enclosed by a double nuclear envelope with pores for mRNA, and containing the nucleolus that makes ribosomal RNA.

Mitochondria feel like animal-cell equipment, and the chloroplast looks like the plant replacement. Plant cells respire too, day and night: they have mitochondria as well - only the chloroplast is plant-only. In the animation the plant cell is drawn with a chloroplast and then a mitochondrion moves in beside it: both organelles belong, because trapping energy and releasing it are two different jobs.

flashcards.front: Name the bond that joins two amino acids in a polypeptide.
Which structure controls the entry and exit of substances in both plant and animal cells?

items.prompt: Which organelles does a mature plant leaf cell contain?
What is the function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum?
items.answer: It is studded with ribosomes and folds proteins for secretion.

items.prompt: A protein is heated and loses its three-dimensional shape while its amino acid sequence stays intact. What is this change called?
Why does a plant cell need mitochondria when it already has chloroplasts?
items.answer: It respires day and night to release energy, and only mitochondria carry out respiration.
